sections.overview: Biotoecus dicentrarchus is a minute geophagine cichlid of the Orinoco basin. It is one of two described Biotoecus species, alongside Amazonian B. opercularis.
sections.identification: Its name refers to its two anal-fin spines, distinguishing it from most cichlids and from its three-spined relative B. opercularis. It is reported to reach about 3.8 cm standard length.
sections.habitat: It occurs in the Orinoco drainage from the Inírida River in Colombia to Maripa in Venezuela. It is recorded from river habitats, although detailed microhabitat data are sparse.
sections.diet: Species-specific diet information was not located in the sources used. Its geophagine relatives forage near the bottom, but finer dietary claims need direct study.
sections.behavior: Available taxonomic summaries offer little behavioral information. The fish is classified as benthopelagic, indicating use of the water column close to the bottom.
sections.reproduction: The consulted references do not provide a verified account of courtship, spawning or parental care. These details cannot safely be inferred from its congener.
sections.ecology: It is the Orinoco member of a genus otherwise represented by Amazonian B. opercularis. The two species differ in drainage and anal-fin spine count.
sections.conservation: The consulted sources describe taxonomy and range but do not establish a current global conservation assessment. Population size and trend remain unclear here.
